newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: S.Leone coup leaders agree to bring back president.
newsitem.headline: S.Leone coup leaders agree to bring back president.

text.p: Negotiators have reached a deal to end a week-long coup in Sierra Leone and bring back deposed civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, a senior diplomat close to the talks said on Sunday.
"The latest is that a deal has been cut. Everything should be in place in a day or two," said the diplomat.
He said rebels fighting a bush war since 1991, who have allied with the coupmakers, were still opposed to a settlement but had not been part of the negotiations.

He said the agreement had all the elements of what the international community had been demanding since junior officers deposed Kabbah a week ago -- "The return of the president, the handover of power by the coupmakers".
Kabbah fled to neighbouring Guinea after the coup.

The diplomat said Kabbah's cabinet would be shuffled to reflect some of the grievances of the coup leaders, who accused him of failing to consolidate a peace deal with rebels of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF) and of causing tension between the country's ethnic groups.

West African states have sent troops to Sierra Leone, ready for a military strike if the talks failed. More than 2,000 foreign residents have been evacuated by sea and air, fleeing looting and violence which followed the takeover.
The coup was deeply unpopular with many Sierra Leoneans, who elected Kabbah last year after four years of army rule.
RUF rebels, recognisable from their matted hair and red headbands, flocked to Freetown to join the coupmakers, who will now have to find a way to remove them.

One Sierra Leonean politician involved in negotiations said relations were already deteriorating before the talks and two people had been killed in gunfights between RUF rebels and coup soldiers inside the military headquarters.
